We need the paginated symptom-definition inventory completed in this small, standard-library-only VCF Operations Go client. Before implementing, research `getSymptomDefinitions` in `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`. Confirm its `/suite-api` base path, method, path, token authentication, query parameters and form-exploded arrays, pagination, response schema, status codes, and defaults. Cite the exact specification URL you consulted in your final answer. Use only this operation.

Implement `(*Client).ListAllSymptomDefinitions` in `client.go`. It must implement exactly the contract operationId `getSymptomDefinitions`: GET `/suite-api/api/symptomdefinitions`, set `Authorization` to the client's token verbatim, set `Accept: application/json`, and send no request body. The query names are exactly `adapterKind`, `resourceKind`, repeated `id` values in input order (OpenAPI form/explode encoding), `name`, `page`, and `pageSize`. Empty scalar string filters and a nil or zero-length ID slice are unset and must be omitted entirely, not serialized as empty query values. Always send the 0-based `page` and effective `pageSize`; `PageSize == 0` uses the specification default 1000, while a negative page size is an error made before any request. Use normal URL query encoding.

Fetch page 0 and continue until the accumulated item count reaches `pageInfo.totalCount`, retaining the full `SymptomDefinition` payload from every page. If the service returns a non-2xx response, malformed JSON, or an empty page before the advertised total is reached, return an error. Honor the supplied context and HTTP client. Before returning, sort the complete collection by `Name` ascending and then `ID` ascending so callers receive stable output independent of server page order.

Keep the public API unchanged and change only `client.go` plus any implementation tests you add. Run `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`. Verification checks exact queries and headers, complete pagination, empty-page protocol failure, context handling, stable sorting, and omission of unset filters.
